definitions.explanation: Having nothing of the same kind that can stand beside it. Used to praise a quality, skill, or enthusiasm that is in a class of its own. Typically appears as {無類|むるい}の + noun, especially in phrases like {無類|むるい}の{酒好|さけず}き ('a peerless lover of sake').

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{無類|むるい}の{酒好|さけず}きだ。
examples.english: He is a peerless lover of sake.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{無類|むるい}の{本好|ほんず}きで、{毎日|まいにち}{読書|どくしょ}をしている。
examples.english: She is a peerless book lover and reads every day.

examples.japanese: この{作家|さっか}は{構想力|こうそうりょく}においては{無類|むるい}の{存在|そんざい}だ。
examples.english: This author is peerless when it comes to imaginative power.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{犬|いぬ}に{対|たい}する{愛情|あいじょう}の{深|ふか}さは{無類|むるい}のもので、{友人|ゆうじん}たちはみんな{感心|かんしん}している。
examples.english: The depth of his love for dogs is unmatched, and his friends are all impressed.

notes:
Composed of {無|む} (without) + {類|るい} (kind, class, category). Literally 'without a (similar) kind' — meaning there is nothing of the same sort with which it can be compared. A formal word most often encountered in the pattern {無類|むるい}の + noun.

TYPICAL PATTERN:
The phrase {無類|むるい}の{Xずき}, where X is a food, drink, or hobby and {ずき} is the 連体形 of {好|す}き, is especially common. It is a set way of saying 'a matchless lover of X.'

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {無類|むるい}の{酒好|さけず}き: a peerless lover of sake
- {無類|むるい}の{甘|あま}いもの{好|ず}き: a peerless lover of sweets
- {無類|むるい}の{犬好|いぬず}き: a peerless dog lover
- {無類|むるい}の{本好|ほんず}き: a peerless book lover
- {無類|むるい}の{強|つよ}さ: unparalleled strength
- {無類|むるい}の{面白|おもしろ}さ: unrivaled fun/interest

REGISTER:
A slightly literary and formal word, but not archaic — it appears in book reviews, profiles, food writing, and everyday praise of a person's enthusiasm. {無類|むるい}の{〜{好|ず}き} in particular is a well-worn cliché that anyone will recognize.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {無比|むひ}: matchless, unparalleled — more formal and literary; usually the second element in compounds like {正確|せいかく}{無比|むひ}. See 23360_muhi.
- {無双|むそう}: matchless, incomparable — old-fashioned, associated with warriors and game titles.
- {類|るい}{まれ}: rare, exceptional — less strong, meaning 'of a rare kind' rather than 'of no kind at all.'
- {比類|ひるい}ない: having no equal — a more neutral, written synonym.

NOTE ON {類|るい}:
The {類|るい} here is the same character used in words like {分類|ぶんるい} (classification) and {種類|しゅるい} (kind). {無類|むるい} literally says 'without a category it belongs to,' meaning nothing else fits in the same bucket.
